tool.name: eScriptorium
tool.command:
## Galaxy runs this command inside the container with `pwd` set to the ## job working directory — every interactive tool gets its own. The ## import/export folders live inside it and are handed to the app ## through IMPORT_DIR / EXPORT_DIR, which import-data.py and the ## export-watcher read at startup. mkdir -p ./exports ./imports ./models && chown -R escriptorium ./exports ./imports ./models || true &&
## Galaxy input datasets -> ./imports (symlinked; auto-imported at ## startup by import-data.py into the "Galaxy import" document) #for $file in $input: ln -sf '$file' "./imports/${file.element_identifier}.${file.ext}" && #end for
## Kraken models -> ./models (symlinked; uploaded as OCR models at ## startup — segmentation vs recognition is detected automatically) #for $model in $kraken_models: ln -sf '$model' "./models/${model.element_identifier}.${model.ext}" && #end for
## Point the app at the dynamically located folders. Everything the ## watcher saves into ./exports is harvested into the history when ## the user ends the session (<discover_datasets> below). export IMPORT_DIR="\$PWD/imports" && export EXPORT_DIR="\$PWD/exports" && export MODEL_DIR="\$PWD/models" &&
## Launch the full stack (postgres, redis, django, celery, nginx) ## in the foreground; Galaxy proxies the entry point to port 80. exec /usr/bin/supervisord -n

param.name: input
param.label: Images / PDF / XML or zip to import
param.help: Datasets are imported into a new document at startup. Leave empty to start from scratch.

param.name: kraken_models
param.label: Kraken models (segmentation / recognition)
param.help: Models are uploaded to eScriptorium at startup and are immediately available in the document's process panel. Segmentation and recognition models are detected automatically.

tool.help:
**eScriptorium** (interactive tool)
Launches a full eScriptorium instance. Input datasets are imported into a document ("Galaxy import") at startup; use the *Images* tab of the document to work with them (segmentation, transcription, model training).
**User story — getting results back into Galaxy:**
1. **Start the tool.** The entry point opens directly in your document: the Galaxy datasets are already imported into the *Galaxy import* document (while the import is running you see a "Preparing your document…" page that reloads automatically). Any Kraken models you passed in are uploaded and ready to use. 2. **Work.** Segment, transcribe and train as usual — everything is saved in the running session. 3. **(Optional) Export individual results while working.** Use the *Export* button on the document dashboard (format, transcription and options of your choice). Every finished export is picked up automatically and saved into the tool's output folder — you can watch it appear on the *Downloads* page. 4. **Close the app.** Click the red **Stop session and export to Galaxy** button in the bottom right corner. This: - triggers a **full export of every document** in the session (all transcriptions + the images — a re-importable backup, e.g. into a later eScriptorium session), - waits for running tasks to finish, - saves all export archives into the Galaxy output folder and shuts the interactive session down. 5. **Collect the results.** When the session ends, Galaxy harvests the output folder into your history as a dataset collection — your per-result exports plus the automatic full-document backup.
**Notes:** - Kraken models passed as inputs land in the *Models* section of the document's process panel; segmentation and recognition models are told apart automatically. - The full backup is exported in ALTO format by default (configurable by the administrator via `STOP_EXPORT_FORMAT`: `alto`, `pagexml` or `json`; set `STOP_EXPORT=no` to disable it). - Exports are asynchronous — after clicking *Export*, wait until the archive appears on the *Downloads* page (or just use the stop button, which waits for it).
